assessments.rationale: Analogy A includes the overheating feedback loop (CPU throttling) which matches the description's feedback component, while Analogy B replaces it with a mere warning, reducing content coverage and structural consistency. Both analogies stay within the same technological domain, so conceptual distance is equal.

Analogy A mentions anticipation of drafts and sunny afternoons, covering the description's external‑perturbation handling, whereas Analogy B omits that clause. This makes A richer in content and more internally coherent, while both remain in the thermostat domain, yielding equal conceptual distance.

Both analogies describe the same greenhouse controller with identical sensor, set‑point, corrective, feedback, and external‑weather handling elements, resulting in identical coverage, structural mapping, and domain distance. Their near‑identical wording suggests a templated reuse.

The two descriptions of the city water supply system are virtually interchangeable, containing the same components and phrasing. Consequently, content coverage, mapping consistency, and conceptual distance are indistinguishable, and the similarity points to a template artifact.

Analogy A directly mirrors physiological temperature regulation, covering all description elements with literal biological mechanisms, giving it higher content coverage and a tighter structural mapping than Analogy B, which uses a traffic system as an adjacent metaphor. The traffic analogy is farther from the biological target, raising its conceptual distance.

Both analogies contain sensing, set‑point comparison, corrective response, feedback, and external‑perturbation handling, so content coverage is equal. The cruise‑control analogy stays within a single mechanical carrier type, making its structural mapping more internally consistent than the financial portfolio analogy, which shifts carriers and adds complexity. The financial analogy is therefore more conceptually distant.
